title: Fix a decorator that runs at the wrong time
blurb: A decorator should record a function once and count its calls. It does neither; find out why and fix it.

brief.why: Uses Decorator syntax, Wrapper functions and When decorators run: write a small program and run its tests.

exercise.title: Fix a decorator that runs at the wrong time
exercise.brief_md:
`tracked` should do two things:

1. add the function's name to `registry` **once, when the function is decorated** (before it is ever called);
2. count **every call** in `wrapper.calls`.

Right now it does neither. **Predict first**: after decorating `ping` and calling it twice, what is in `registry`, and what is `ping.calls`? Then run the tests, find which lines run at the wrong time, and fix them.

```python
@tracked
def ping():
    return "pong"

registry        # ["ping"] straight after the def
ping(); ping()
ping.calls      # 2
```
exercise.solution_walkthrough_md: The decorator's own body runs once, when `@tracked` is applied (at the `def`). The wrapper's body runs on every call. So the registration moves out of the wrapper into `tracked` itself, and the counter goes inside the wrapper.

tests.name: registers at decoration time
tests.fail_md: Nothing was recorded when the function was decorated: code that should run once at the `def` is sitting inside the wrapper.

tests.name: counts every call
tests.fail_md: The counter never moves: the wrapper runs on every call, so that is where the count has to go up.

tests.name: calls do not register again
tests.fail_md: The name is added on every call. Registration belongs to decoration time, which happens once.

tests.name: passes arguments and returns the result
tests.fail_md: The wrapper must pass every argument through and return what the original function returns.

tests.name: each function has its own counter
tests.fail_md: The count is shared between functions: keep it on each wrapper, not in one global.

tests.name: same as the manual form
tests.code:
registry.clear()
def g():
    return 5
g = tracked(g)
assert registry == ["g"] and g() == 5 and g.calls == 1
tests.fail_md: `@tracked` above `def g` is the same as `g = tracked(g)`: both must register once and count calls.

hints: Which lines run when `@tracked` is applied, and which run each time you call the function?
Move the line that records the name out of `wrapper`, into `tracked` itself.
